delta.description: Signed. Never zero — a movement that moves nothing is a record with no fact behind it.

AttributeAllowedValueDTO.description: An option for a select-typed attribute.

AttributeDataType.description: The data type of a back-office-authored attribute — drives the form input + value column.

AttributeValidationDTO.description: Optional per-attribute validation envelope (jsonb `validation`). All fields optional.

AttributeValueInputDTO.description: A value supplied for one attribute on create/edit (only the field matching the data type is set).

CatalogSchemaDTO.description: One call bootstraps the create form: the active types (each with their assigned attributes) and the active category tree (flat, parentId-linked).

CategoryDTO.description: A node in the platform category taxonomy (flat list; the tree is built client-side via parentId).

CreatePresignedUploadRequest.description: POST /shop/v1/products/{id}/media — request a presigned direct-to-S3 upload.

CreateProductRequest.description: POST /shop/v1/products — create a shop-owned product. `brand` is a first-class column (FR-010a).

weightGrams.description: Shipping weight in grams (032, FR-036a). Omit and the platform records its stated default as an ASSUMPTION. ⚠ There is deliberately no `weightIsAssumed` field: the flag is derived from the act of supplying a weight and is never accepted from a client, or "measured" would mean only "the client said so".

DeliveryPromiseDTO.description:
What the customer bought and when this shop must be ready — READ-ONLY (FR-009a).

Owned by 021. While only one service level exists, `readyBy` is a constant offset from the order's placement, so ordering by promise IS ordering by arrival (FR-001b, SC-020).

Says NOTHING about who delivers. There is no carrier, driver, or provider field here, by design.

readyBy.description: ISO-8601. The time by which THIS shop must be ready.

serviceLevel.description: e.g. "standard". A service level the customer bought — never a fulfillment mechanism.

FulfillmentDeliveryDTO.description: The delivery context a shop needs to prepare and label the order (FR-009). Snapshotted onto the order at placement by 019, so it never changes retroactively.

items.description: THIS shop's lines only. Never another shop's, and never an order-level total.

FulfillmentItemDTO.description:
One line to pick. Quantities are absolute, never deltas.

`orderedQuantity - gatheredQuantity` on a terminal portion is the SHORTFALL — what the customer paid for and will not receive. It carries no financial effect in this slice (FR-010b) and exists to be resolved by a later refunds slice, which is why it must stay queryable rather than implied.

FulfillmentQueueState.description: Which slice of the queue to read (FR-016).

FulfillmentStatus.description:
The fulfillment state machine (FR-011).

`pending` is written by the 019 fan-out. `received` was reserved by 019 and unused until now — it means a human acknowledged the order, which is what distinguishes untouched work from work in progress. `collected` (picked up) and `delivered` are reachable ONLY via the dev-only driver stubs (FR-030) and are terminal + immutable (FR-011f) — a placeholder for the real driver slice.

FulfillmentSummaryDTO.description: A row in the shop's order queue (GET /shop/v1/fulfillments).

atRisk.description: Computed against the promise — drives in-place escalation, never reordering (FR-001a, SC-018).

id.description: shop_fulfillment.id — the portion, not the order.

itemCount.description: Items THIS shop must gather. Never the order's total item count.

placedAt.description: ISO-8601, when the customer placed the order.

stateChangedAt.description: ISO-8601, when the portion last changed state — drives time-in-state (FR-011c).

ItemProgressRequest.description:
Record picking progress (PATCH /shop/v1/fulfillments/{id}/items/{orderItemId}).

Absolute values, not deltas — idempotent under retry, which matters on a shop tablet with a flaky connection. Lowering `unavailableQuantity` is how an item is un-flagged when it turns up (FR-010d). `gathered + unavailable <= ordered` is enforced server-side and by a DB CHECK.

severity.description: "out" sorts above "low" — an empty shelf is not the same problem as a thin one.

PickupStubRequest.description:
⚠ DEV-ONLY SCAFFOLD (POST /shop/v1/fulfillments/{id}/pickup) — FR-030…FR-034.

Stands in for a driver collecting the order so the lifecycle is exercisable before a driver surface exists. The endpoint is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT outside local development (FR-031): it accepts a caller-supplied identity, so a reachable deployed instance would be an order-state forgery primitive. Scheduled for deletion when the driver slice ships (FR-034).

driverRef.description: Stored MARKED AS A PLACEHOLDER so stub collections never resemble a real dispatch (FR-033).

ProblemFieldIssue.description: RFC 9457 problem+json — the platform's single machine-readable error shape (mirrors docs/api/error-envelope.md from 004). Typed ONCE here (Principle II); every web surface consumes it, never re-declares it.

field.description:
The offending field path — or, for a whole-request refusal, a STABLE MACHINE-READABLE CODE.

⚠ 032 uses the second form for delivery-pricing refusals (`cap_below_floor`, `bands_required`, …). "Please check the fields and try again" tells an operator nothing about which of five rules they broke, and every one of those rules fails SILENTLY in production if it is not understood — a cap below the floor makes every delivery cost the cap, forever.

ProductAttributeValueDTO.description: A typed attribute value on a product (EAV, one value shape per data type).

ProductDetailDTO.description: Full product detail. `updatedAt` is the optimistic-concurrency token (FR-023a); `missingMandatoryAttributes` is the non-blocking schema-drift notice (FR-020a).

weightGrams.description: Shipping weight in grams (032). ⚠ A LOGISTICS fact, deliberately distinct from any `net_weight` attribute a shopper reads on the product page — they agree by backfill today and may legitimately diverge, because packaging weighs something. Delivery is priced from this.

weightIsAssumed.description: ⚠ TRUE means nobody has recorded a real weight and the platform default is in use. Without this flag "500 g" would mean both "we weighed it" and "nobody has said", and no operator could tell which products still need attention (FR-037a).

ProductListDTO.description: Paged product list envelope. Structurally a `PagedDTO<ProductListItemDTO>` but declared concretely (not a generic alias) so the Kotlin contract generator can name it.

ProductListItemDTO.description: A thin row in the shop catalog table (backend-paginated).

ProductMediaDTO.description: A media object on a product (list/detail carry short-lived presigned GET urls).

ProductStockDTO.description: A product's stock, as one operator screen needs it.

effectiveThreshold.description: Product threshold, else shop default, else null — null meaning nothing counts as low.

low.description: tracked && effectiveThreshold !== null && onHand > 0 && onHand <= effectiveThreshold. ⚠ Mutually exclusive with `outOfStock`: an empty shelf and a thin one are different problems needing different actions, and collapsing them tells the operator nothing to act on.

onHand.description: null exactly when untracked — the database makes "tracked with no count" unrepresentable.

threshold.description: This product's own threshold, or null to fall back to the shop default.

tracked.description: false = unlimited, and identical to how the product behaved before 054 existed (FR-002).

ProductTypeAttributeDTO.description: An attribute assigned to a product type (the join, carrying the per-type facts).

ProductTypeDTO.description: A back-office product classification, with its assigned attributes.

RequestableTransition.description:
Advance or reverse a portion (POST /shop/v1/fulfillments/{id}/status).

Only `picking` and `ready_for_pickup` are requestable: `pending` is the fan-out's, `received` is implicit on first open (FR-011a), and `collected` belongs to the pickup stub alone (FR-030). `ready_for_pickup -> picking` is the ONE permitted reversal (FR-011d).

SchemaStatus.description: Lifecycle for the managed schema entities (product types, attributes, categories).

SetProductSectionsRequest.description: PATCH /shop/v1/products/{id}/sections — set a product's section membership.

threshold.description: null clears this product's own threshold, falling back to the shop default.

onHand.description: REQUIRED when enabling (FR-003), ignored when disabling.

ShopLifecycleStatus.description: Shop lifecycle status (009-shop-management). Only `active` shops serve their operators; `suspended` (temporary hold) and `disabled` (deactivated, retained for audit) both refuse.

ShopRole.description: Shop RBAC roles. Prefixed so `manager` stays unambiguously the back-office role in logs.

ShopSectionDTO.description: A shop-local section (grouping; Uber-Eats-style menu section).

ShopStaffRecordDTO.description: Wire DTO for GET /shop/v1/me (contracts/shop-me.contract.md). `email` may be null until provisioning supplies it; `shop` is null for an unassigned operator — an expected state, not an error.

ShopStaffStatus.description: Platform-owned lifecycle. A disabled operator is denied despite an otherwise-valid token.

defaultThreshold.description: null = no default, so nothing counts as low; zero stock is still reported as out (FR-005a).

ShopSummaryDTO.description: Wire DTO for the assigned shop, embedded in GET /shop/v1/me.

StockActorKind.description:
WHO acted, kept separate from WHY (`reason`).

⚠ The separation is what makes FR-027 possible: a shop reading its own history must be able to see plainly that back-office made a change, without back-office having to pick a reason that says so. `system` is the paid-order path — the only actor with no person behind it.

actorLabel.description: A display name where the platform holds one. ⚠ Never an email address (no PII in an audit read).

orderNumber.description: The order that caused it, by its customer-facing reference. null for a human's own change.

StockMovementReason.description:
Why a count moved. A CLOSED set, mirroring the CHECK on `public.stock_movement.reason` — the database and this union are one contract, and a value in either that the other lacks is a defect.

⚠ There is deliberately NO `cancellation` or `refund` member. Neither capability exists on the platform (order-flow gap register, Tier 2), and a value nothing can produce implies one that does. The set grows when the slice that needs it lands.

UpdateMediaRequest.description: PATCH /shop/v1/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} — reorder / set primary / alt text.

UpdateProductRequest.description: PATCH /shop/v1/products/{id} — focused edit. All content fields optional (a subset is patched); `expectedUpdatedAt` is REQUIRED (optimistic concurrency — a stale value → 409, FR-023a).

weightGrams.description: Recording a weight here marks it MEASURED (032, FR-036a). Omit to leave it as it stands.

description: Aggregator — codegen entry only. Every field forces a type into the schema. The catalog block is the shop-facing subset (016) the mobile app consumes; admin-only schema-authoring request DTOs are deliberately NOT here.
title: ShopContract
